import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):

        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels

        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)

analyses.1: There are no recipe trials yet. The default recipe takes only 131k steps in 4096-sample updates, which is just 32 policy updates. The 4 baseline seeds scored 0.068 three times and 0.258 once, so the run seems to either break through or stall, and that looks like an optimisation problem. My guess is that too few on-policy updates is the main bottleneck. Two levers can raise the update count within the compute budget: smaller rollout batches per update, and fewer PPO epochs, since fewer epochs also buy more environment steps (2 epochs gives about 243k steps, 1 epoch about 426k). Round 1 tests three settings of these levers. One also lowers entropy, because about 400 legal actions with ent_coef 0.01 may keep the policy too spread out for exact greedy builds. Another raises gamma so the +1 exact-build bonus counts for more. A gap smaller than about 0.1 between 2-seed means should be treated as noise.
analyses.2: All three round-1 recipes scored exactly 0.0684 on both seeds, which is 35 of 512 designs. Three of the baseline's four seeds landed on the same number, and training success sits near 0.069 too. So 0.0684 is a plateau where training gets stuck, not noise. Changing batch size, epochs, data volume and gamma never left it. The baseline's one lucky seed (0.258) shows a better solution exists. The likely cause is that exploration collapses early. To succeed, the agent must find rare events: pressing DONE (one of about 400 actions) at exactly the right moment, and placing bricks in the right order. This round therefore tests exploration levers: a much higher entropy bonus, a lower learning rate so the policy collapses more slowly, and large batches so each update contains more rare successes. Each run takes under 60 s, so time is not a constraint.
analyses.3: Almost every trial stays at exactly 0.0684 on both seeds. That looks like one stable local optimum, probably a fixed habit of when to stop or which bricks to place, not gradual progress. Only two runs have escaped it: one default-recipe seed (0.258) and one seed with ent_coef 0.03 (0.334). The recipes that cut epochs to get more samples, used low entropy or a low learning rate, or used larger or smaller batches all stayed stuck, including one at ent_coef 0.02. So sample count does not seem to limit learning. Keeping exploration up while still taking strong updates (4 epochs) seems to matter. The r2c1 result is one lucky seed out of two, which is weak evidence. This round refines r2c1 one change at a time: more entropy, longer credit assignment for the +1 exact-build bonus, and a larger step size. Each run keeps 4 epochs and the default batch.
analyses.4: Every trial with ent_coef 0.01 or less, or with lr 3e-4, stayed on the 0.068 plateau. Raising entropy to 0.03–0.05 at the default lr gave mixed seeds (0.20–0.22 means). Adding lr 0.002 to ent 0.03 lifted both seeds to 0.33 and 0.42 (mean 0.375), which is the clearest result so far. Longer credit (gamma 0.99) hurt, and so did single-epoch schemes and huge-batch schemes. So getting off the plateau seems to need strong exploration plus large, decisive updates. This is the last round, and the top three trials each get two more seeds, so each candidate is a small, robust step around r3c3: a higher lr, more entropy, and more frequent updates with the same total gradient work. Seed noise is still large (±0.1–0.15), so I will read any single 2-seed difference with care.
